statement: REDSEC combat mechanics taken from EA's official REDSEC armor community update. Only mechanics stated by that source are encoded here. Anything the source does not state is listed under `unresolved` and is never invented.

battleRoyale.evidence: EA: "Armor in Battle Royale: 80 HP total (2 plates at 40 HP each)".

gauntlet.evidence: EA: "Gauntlet armor: 40 HP". Recorded for completeness; Gauntlet is not a selectable target state in this application.

soldierHealth.claimVerified: REDSEC soldier health is the same standard Battlefield 6 soldier-health pool used by Multiplayer, and weapons deal the same health damage at the same ranges.
soldierHealth.evidence: EA: "Once armor breaks, that weapon will deal the same damage to soldier health, at the same ranges, as it does in the rest of Battlefield 6." EA also describe armour as "extra health layered on top of your standard soldier health", and state the guiding principle is to "leave core gun mechanics and soldier health damage the same across experiences" and tune REDSEC by adjusting damage vs. armor instead.
soldierHealth.note: EA do not print a health number, but the claim this project relies on is equality with Multiplayer, which they state directly. The numeric pool (100 HP) comes from this project's own audited Multiplayer model, not from the REDSEC source. There is therefore nothing unresolved here.

damageVsArmor.principle: Each caliber effectively has two damage curves: Damage vs. Soldier Health and Damage vs. Armor. Only the damage-vs-armor curve is adjusted; the soldier-health curve is untouched.
damageVsArmor.evidence: EA: "each caliber effectively has two damage curves: Damage vs. Soldier Health and Damage vs. Armor" and "In REDSEC, we only adjust weapon damage against armor."

rangeShiftMeters.evidence: EA: "For damage vs. armor, we shift those drop-off thresholds outward by 10 meters." The damage values themselves are not restated, so the same step damages are used at the shifted ranges. No damage value is scaled or invented.

removeFirstCloseRangeStep.evidence: EA: "For automatic weapons we reduce or remove the very close-range maximum damage step when calculating damage vs. armor", and elsewhere "the very close-range damage is flattened". The source states the rule qualitatively and publishes no per-caliber damage-vs-armor table, so the exact treatment (fully removed versus partially reduced, and by how much) is not established.
removeFirstCloseRangeStep.implementedReading: The leading maximum-damage step is dropped entirely, so the second step's damage applies from 0 m. This is the literal reading of "removed"/"flattened" and requires no invented number. The alternative reading ("reduced" by some unpublished amount) would need a value the source does not provide, so it is not implemented.
removeFirstCloseRangeStep.fireModeSource: data/weapons.json fireMode field; 'auto' is the only fire mode that is unambiguously an automatic weapon. Burst, semi, bolt and pump weapons receive the range shift only.

generalisationScope.note: EA published a worked example for one calibre only. The rule is stated generally for 'automatic weapons', so it is applied to every fireMode:auto weapon, but no per-calibre armour table has been published or extracted. Treat per-weapon close-range armour damage as DERIVED, not verified.

unresolved.mechanic: Exact damage-vs-armor values for the close-range step of automatic weapons
unresolved.why: EA states the rule as "reduce or remove" and publishes no damage-vs-armor table for any caliber. Reduce and remove give different armored BTK at close range.
evidenceChecked: targeted search for datamined per-caliber armor curves
unresolved.wouldNeed: A published or extracted per-caliber damage-vs-armor table, or reproducible in-game measurement.

unresolved.mechanic: Spillover of leftover damage when a shot destroys armor
unresolved.why: Not addressed by the source. Armor damage and health damage are different scales, so converting leftover armor damage into health damage would require an unpublished conversion rule.
evidenceChecked: EA REDSEC armor community update (ea.com) and its EA Forums / se7en mirrors
Targeted searches for overkill / carry-over / plate-break damage behaviour
raymdl/BF6-Weapon-Analyzer upstream repository - contains no REDSEC or armour data
Steam community discussion on REDSEC plates - opinion only, no instrumented testing
unresolved.wouldNeed: An explicit statement or measurement of whether excess damage carries into health.
unresolved.implementedPolicyRationale: Modelling no spillover requires no invented conversion between the armor and health damage scales. Modelling spillover would. The conservative choice is therefore the one that invents nothing.

modelledInterpretations.none: Implemented default. The shot that destroys armour damages armour only; the next shot begins on health.
modelledInterpretations.proportional: Alternative used for sensitivity analysis only. The fraction of the shot's armour damage not needed to break armour carries into health, scaled by that same shot's health-damage value. Both numbers come from the bullet itself, so no constant is invented.

unresolved.mechanic: Headshot and limb multipliers against armor
evidenceChecked: EA REDSEC armor community update and its mirrors
unresolved.wouldNeed: Published or measured hit-location multipliers against armor.
unresolved.note: This application ranks on chest damage only, so no headshot behaviour is claimed for REDSEC.

unresolved.mechanic: Whether the two 40 HP plates behave as two discrete pools or one 80 HP pool
evidenceChecked: EA REDSEC armor community update and its mirrors
unresolved.wouldNeed: A statement or measurement of per-plate break behaviour.
unresolved.note: Under the implemented no-spillover policy the two readings produce identical BTK and TTK, so this does not currently affect any displayed result. The model stores plates as an ordered list so per-plate behaviour can be added later.

confidence.reason: Armour HP, the +10 m range shift and the post-armour health path are verified. The close-range automatic rule is DERIVED from a single published calibre example, and the armour-break transition is unverified. Per-result confidence is computed from whether those two mechanics actually change that specific result.

sources.note: Used to corroborate the transcription of the ea.com article.
Corroboration of wording only. Not used as independent evidence for any value.

structuralCrossCheck.note: EA's worked example uses the same step boundaries as the repository's synced damage curve for the same caliber, confirming that this project's stepped dmg arrays are the curves the range-shift rule applies to. Damage values differ slightly because the repository curve is the pinned Sym.gg 1.3.3.0 game-file snapshot and EA's article quotes a later balance state; no value from the article is copied into the data.

loadout.structure: REDSEC Battle Royale does not use a standard Multiplayer pre-match loadout. In the infiltration helicopter the player chooses Class, Training Path, starting Sidearm and Melee weapon only.
loadout.signatureSet: The chosen Class brings a fixed Class Signature Set: two gadgets, a Signature Weapon Proficiency and a Signature Trait. These come with the class rather than being individually chosen.
loadout.primaryAcquisition: Players drop with a sidearm and melee only, and loot primaries from the world, Class Chests, Missions and Custom Weapon Drops. A Class Chest most frequently contains a highly-upgraded weapon of that class's Signature Weapon type.
loadout.productImplication: The weapon recommendation for REDSEC is what to seek and use once found, not something equipped before the match. The application must not imply a Multiplayer-style pre-match primary loadout in REDSEC.
evidence: EA REDSEC Battle Royale 101: "While in the infiltration helicopter, choose your Class, Training Path (for active and passive Gadgets and abilities), Starting Sidearm, and Melee Weapon."

EA REDSEC guide: "Instead of a Primary Weapon, Sidearm, customizable Gadgets and more, you are limited to the following items: Your Class, which comes with a Class Signature Set - Two Gadgets, a Signature Weapon Proficiency and a Signature Trait - and a four-trait Training Path."
EA REDSEC guide: "Choose a Class, drop in with a Sidearm, loot better weapons..."
EA REDSEC guide on Class Chests: "A Class chest will most frequently include a highly-upgraded weapon from the Class' Signature Weapon, such as an LMG for the Support Class."

transformFixture.purpose: Validates the damage-vs-armor transform against the only worked example EA has published. These numbers are EA's article values for a later balance state and are deliberately NOT copied into data/weapons.json, which stays the pinned Sym.gg snapshot.

spilloverResolutionTest.purpose: Settle the armour-break transition with the fewest shots. Both cases use weapons that are NOT automatic, so the derived close-range rule is not applied to them and the test isolates the spillover mechanic alone.
spilloverResolutionTest.howToRead: Count the total bullets needed to down a full-armour (2 plate, 80 HP) target that is not healing. The two candidate models predict different totals, so the shot count alone settles it.

primaryCase.attachments: Any. No attachment in the current data changes chest damage; use Standard ammo so no ammo modifier is involved.
primaryCase.distanceM: 40 to 60 (anywhere in this band gives the same prediction, so exact ranging is not required)
primaryCase.targetState: Full armour, 2 plates, 80 HP, undamaged health
primaryCase.aimAt: Chest / torso only. Do not headshot: head multipliers against armour are unverified and would invalidate the test.
primaryCase.distinguishes: 6 shots to down = NO spillover (current implementation). 5 shots to down = damage carries across the armour break.

highContrastCase.targetState: Full armour, 2 plates, 80 HP, undamaged health
highContrastCase.distinguishes: 4 shots = NO spillover. 3 shots = spillover. Highest contrast of any case found: the armour-breaking shot has 74.4 of 77.2 armour damage unused.

alsoRecord: The damage numbers shown in the personal damage log for each individual shot, if the HUD exposes them.
Whether the armour bar and the health bar both move on the same shot.
Whether the result differs when the first plate breaks versus when the second plate breaks (this would indicate per-plate rather than single-pool behaviour).
spilloverResolutionTest.caveat: Predicted shot counts use this project's pinned Sym.gg damage snapshot, which is a slightly different balance state from EA's published article values. If the observed count matches neither prediction, record the per-shot damage numbers rather than assuming a spillover model.
